name: Nuclear and Strategic Deterrence
measurement_scope: Strategic nuclear posture, survivability, command-and-control resilience, and associated strategic capabilities
primary_indicator_family: Nuclear forces, delivery systems, survivability, C2, strategic doctrine
notes: Recognition must distinguish weapons capability, peaceful nuclear capability, and legitimate nuclear-system participation. Public data are incomplete by construction.

name: Conventional Military Power
measurement_scope: Conventional force structure, readiness, logistics, technology, sustainment, and operational capacity
primary_indicator_family: Force structure, defence expenditure, readiness, logistics, platforms, munitions, deployment capacity
notes: Avoid treating expenditure as capability itself; expenditure is an input indicator.

name: Economic Production
measurement_scope: Scale, productivity, diversification, productive capacity, and macroeconomic resilience
primary_indicator_family: GDP, industrial output, productivity, trade, fiscal capacity
notes: Use multiple indicators rather than GDP alone.

name: Financial and Monetary Power
measurement_scope: Domestic financial depth and international monetary, payments, reserve, and capital-market capacity
primary_indicator_family: Currency internationalization, reserves, banking depth, capital markets, payment systems
notes: Distinguish domestic financial size from systemic international financial centrality.

name: Science and Technology
measurement_scope: Scientific research, technological capability, engineering depth, innovation, and technology deployment
primary_indicator_family: R&D, publications, patents, high-technology output, frontier research, engineering capacity
notes: Indicators must distinguish quantity from technological quality and strategic relevance.

name: Advanced Industrial Capacity
measurement_scope: Ability to design, manufacture, scale, maintain, and upgrade advanced industrial systems
primary_indicator_family: Manufacturing, machine tools, semiconductors, aerospace, chemicals, advanced materials, industrial supply chains
notes: Industrial capability is broader than manufacturing output.

name: Energy and Resource Security
measurement_scope: Reliable access to energy and strategic resources together with resilience to disruption
primary_indicator_family: Energy production, imports, reserves, grids, refining, critical minerals, diversification
notes: Security depends on both resource endowment and resilience/diversification.

name: Food
primary_indicator_family: Capacity to sustain populations and absorb food, water, health, and humanitarian shocks
notes: Food production, water security, health capacity, strategic reserves, emergency response
column7: Humanitarian resilience is not equivalent to agricultural output alone.

name: Infrastructure and Logistics
measurement_scope: Physical and digital infrastructure supporting movement, production, communication, and recovery
primary_indicator_family: Ports, rail, roads, airports, electricity, telecommunications, logistics networks
notes: Network topology and redundancy matter alongside physical stock.

name: Diplomatic and Institutional Power
measurement_scope: Capacity to shape international institutions, coalitions, negotiations, norms, and crisis management
primary_indicator_family: Diplomatic network, treaty participation, institutions, mediation, alliance connectivity
notes: Do not reduce diplomacy to number of embassies.

name: Information
primary_indicator_family: Information infrastructure, cyber capability, AI research and deployment, and digital-system resilience
notes: AI compute and research, cyber institutions, digital infrastructure, information systems
column7: Separate defensive resilience, offensive capability, research capacity, and civilian digital capacity where evidence permits.

name: Civilizational and Social Resilience
measurement_scope: Social cohesion, institutional legitimacy, demographic resilience, adaptive capacity, and continuity under stress
primary_indicator_family: Demographics, education, social indicators, institutional trust, crisis adaptation, continuity measures
notes: Avoid subjective civilizational ranking; operationalize resilience through observable indicators.
